qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Deliberate scarcity model and Formula 1 heritage volume automakers cannot copy without self-cannibalization. Proof of moat: 25%+ ROIC across economic cycles, ~50% gross margins, 38%+ EBITDA margins, and a 2+ year sold-out order backlog. Extreme pricing power demonstrated by personalization options contributing over 19% of revenues. Key erosion threats include brand dilution if volume expands beyond luxury scarcity limits, powertrain sound/emotional shift in the transition to hybrid/EVs, and European small-volume emissions derogation changes.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (FCF conversion < 80%, REJECT). Despite possessing one of the world's most formidable luxury moats (30Y CAP, 25%+ ROIC, multi-year order backlogs), Ferrari fails Pillar 2 FCF conversion: 5-year cumulative Industrial FCF / Net Income is ~68.4% (67.3% in 2024, 74.1% in 2023), missing the strict 80% cash conversion threshold due to continuous heavy automotive manufacturing capex and capitalized development outlays for new model architectures.
qualitative.evidence: Ferrari generated €1,526M net income and €1,027M industrial FCF in 2024 (67.3% conversion), and €1,257M net income and €932M industrial FCF in 2023 (74.1% conversion). Cumulative 2020-2024 industrial FCF of €3,531M against net income of €5,164M yields 68.4% conversion, failing the Gate 6 80% threshold. Operating ROIC exceeds 25%, gross margins exceed 49%, and order books are fully committed through 2026. Consolidated gross debt stands at €3.35B (including €1.66B financial services debt) against €3.53B equity and €1.74B cash.
